wave: Wave 15 — Adversarial Red-Team Audit Track 2 (PQC, Symmetric & ZK SOTA Catches)

adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.target_claim: Mitigation 3A & QDS-8: Select-SWAP (QROAM) with B=8 reduces M=512, w=32 scan from 16,384 to 576 Toffolis (28.4x) in CSIDH-512 / UOV / BIKE.
adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.the_catch_or_bug: Low-Kliuchnikov-Schaeffer [2018] QROAM ((M/B) + 2Bw Toffolis) ONLY works when the M-word table is CLASSICAL (so the Select step uses 0-Toffoli CNOT fan-out from unary address lines). When the M words are QUANTUM registers in superposition (e.g., QDS-8 dynamic Patricia Crit-Bit Trie mutated during UOV/BIKE/Kuperberg sieving), copying a quantum word into the B-word buffer requires CCX (Toffoli) gates on EVERY bit (M*w = 16,384 Toffolis) PLUS another M*w = 16,384 Toffolis to uncompute the entangled table (33,280 Toffolis total — 2.03x WORSE than direct full-scan CSWAP!). Furthermore, CSIDH-512 only has M = 74 static odd primes (not 512), costing 10 + 512 = 522 Toffolis via classical QROAM.

adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.target_claim: Mitigation 3B & QDS-7: One-Way Pivot-XOR R_i <- R_i ^ (s_p & R_p) + elimination cuts McEliece ISD Toffolis by 1/3 (536M -> 358M) with 0 history matrix.
adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.the_catch_or_bug: 1) Overwrite Bug: s_p = (~M_{i,i}) & ... & M_{p,i} depends on M_{i,i}. Executing R_i <- R_i ^ (s_p & R_p) overwrites M'_{i,i} = 1, destroying the original M_{i,i} so s_p CANNOT be uncomputed from column i in-place! 2) Self-Control Bug: Downward elimination R_p <- R_p ^ (M_{p,i} & R_i) cannot simultaneously control on M_{p,i} and clear M_{p,i} <- 0 without copying M_{p,i} to an ancilla or preserving it in L. 3) Ancilla Explosion: Retaining the uncomputable pivot-selection indicators s_{i,p} until the end of the Grover oracle requires r(r-1)/2 = 768*767/2 = 294,528 ancilla qubits for Classic McEliece-348864 (r = 768)!

adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.target_claim: QDS-7 & Mitigation 3B: Classic McEliece-348864 Prange/Bruhat ISD runs in 4,820 Q (or 768 Q) and 358M Toffolis.
adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.the_catch_or_bug: Scale Mismatch Bug: Classic McEliece-348864 has n = 3488, k = 2720, so codimension r = n - k = 768. Storing a single 768 x 768 binary submatrix in quantum registers requires 768^2 = 589,824 qubits (590,592 Q with syndrome/latch, matching Perriello et al. [2023, ePrint 2023/1065] and Esser et al. [2022, Eurocrypt], or 884,352 Q if retaining 294,528 One-Way Pivot-XOR indicators). Our 4,820 Q number was for a reduced r = 64 toy submatrix (64^2 + 724 = 4,820 Q), undercounting full r = 768 matrix qubits by 122.37x while pairing it with r = 768 Toffoli counts!

adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.target_claim: Mitigation 4: K=4 sub-pipelining achieves 378 Q compute on AES-256 at 4x depth penalty; K=32 achieves 1,826 Q on SHA3-256 at 10x depth penalty.
adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.the_catch_or_bug: 1) Published SOTA Comparison: Zou et al. [2020, ASIACRYPT] and Huang & Sun [2022, ASIACRYPT] ALREADY achieve 376 Q - 400 Q for AES-256 at 1x round depth (NO 4x intra-round depth penalty!) by using rolling in-place key expansion and uncomputing round ancillas at the round boundary. 2) Hidden 1.75x S-Box Toffoli Overhead in K=4 Sub-Pipelining: Reusing K=4 Boyar-Peralta S-Box scratch blocks (88 Q) across the 4 columns of a single AES round requires uncomputing the 22 Q intermediate ANDs after Columns 0, 1, and 2 (costing 2 * 34 = 68 ANDs/byte on 12 bytes + 34 ANDs/byte on 4 bytes = 952 ANDs/round vs. 544 ANDs/round = 1.75x gate blowup!).

adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.target_claim: SOTA Non-Constructive / Zero-Knowledge / QROM Existence Proofs (Zhandry 2019, Watrous 2009, Unruh 2012, Kuperberg 2005/2013).
adversarial_catch_and_sota_table.the_catch_or_bug: 1) Zhandry [2019, Crypto] Compressed Random Oracle (QROM): Existence proofs count Q queries using O(Q*w) database qubits. Constructively without QRAM, the compressed database is a dynamic quantum superposition table (Catch 4 Case 2), so query q must scan and CSWAP-sort all q active slots, costing sum_{q=1}^Q 2*q*w = Q(Q+1)w Toffolis (537,395,200 Toffolis for Q=1024, w=512 — a 1,025x per-query gate blowup!). 2) Watrous [2009] vs. Unruh [2012] Quantum ZK: Watrous coherent rewinding requires 2k+1 coherent executions of V* and (V*)^dag with 0 intermediate measurement; Unruh's QROM NIZK transform avoids inverting V* but requires t*M_open = 128*3 = 384 parallel hash commitments (14,745,600 SHA3-256 Toffolis). 3) Kuperberg [2005, 2013] CSIDH-512 Sieve: While the M=74 static primes use classical QROAM (522 Toffolis), collimating a quantum sieve table of L=1,024 superposition states (w=512 bits) costs L*w = 524,288 Toffolis per step (1,004x higher than classical QROAM!).
